learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solve engineering problems.
Describe motion and its causes in oscillatory systems.
Apply knowledge of oscillatory systems when spatial propagation exists through different media.
Theoretically describe the electric field. Calculate its expressions by applying the most appropriate laws in each situation.
Understand the movement of charges over time.
Relate moving electric charges to a magnetic field and describe the forces they are subjected to.
Theoretically describe the magnetic field. Calculate its expressions by applying the most appropriate laws in each situation.
Relate the electric and magnetic fields to a common origin.

assessment_rules: The final written exam is mandatory. If only the final exam is taken, it accounts for 100% of the grade. If one, two, or three of the other optional activities (each valued at 10%) are completed, then the final exam will account for 90%, 80%, or 70% respectively. Approved activities are saved for subsequent calls until December. The exam consists of 6 questions (5 problems, 1 theoretical), and the presentation, theoretical approach, and correct conclusion are valued.
